correctness.rationale: The induced-character 2x2 blocks give all 4m regular dimensions. Same-coset zero fibers have nullity two, mixed-coset zero fibers nullity one; cubic roots have exactly the counted numbers of cyclic-character preimages. The dihedral/dicyclic gcd ratio equals two exactly when v2(u)>v2(m). Counting anchored same-coset triples and mixed displacements yields exact closed integer counts. Independent direct regular-matrix ranks over QQ match every support in Q_4m for 2<=m<=9 and both Q_4m and D_4m at m=3,6; exhaustive combinatorial parity comparisons cover 2<=m<=12. Finite checks are only confirmations; the all-m proof is algebraic.

originality.rationale: The prior general dicyclic determinant and representation formulas are acknowledged as dominant methodological inputs, and singularity alone is not claimed novel. The inspected primary works and published three-tap records do not state the paired, pointwise dihedral-versus-dicyclic parity-halving law for complex nullities, or the exact number of supports where nullity halves. The older dihedral classification does not by itself determine twisted-kernel dimensions. An implicit derivation from broader general formulas and unknown earlier exact specializations are residual risks.
residual_risks: Paudel–Pinner and predecessor group-determinant identities are broad enough to permit this classification after nontrivial case and multiplicity analysis; an earlier implicit or explicit specialization may exist.

The published dihedral three-tap theorem has identical singular-support incidence and total counts after cyclic-order substitution; novelty is confined to the twisted positive nullities and strictly-halved stratum, not a claim of a new singular set.

A bibliographically unlocated treatment of singular dicyclic Cayley digraphs or dicyclic three-sparse group-ring elements may already contain this comparison. Independent mathematical validation has not occurred.

value.rationale: A natural, complete singular convolution-kernel invariant is determined for all three-element unweighted supports on a central nonsplit versus split index-two cyclic extension. Twisting does not move a single singular three-tap support, but it erases exactly half its kernel directions on a mathematically characterized 2-adic/3-adic resonance class. The explicit factor-of-two boundary and its closed support census quantify nontrivial structural spectral behavior, rather than a renamed known result or a routine finite-table entry.
